suppress.notes: TIER 1. org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql is a Java test support module: it starts a PostgreSQL container for integration tests and contains no database engine code whatsoever. Dependency-Check matched its Maven version 2.0.3 against cpe:/a:postgresql:postgresql, that is against PostgreSQL SERVER version 2.0.3, and attached the server advisory history for that version to it. Twenty six records at CVSS 7 or above arrived this way, the oldest from 2015. The mismatch is a property of the artifact, not of any one advisory, so the CPE is removed rather than the CVEs. The actual PostgreSQL server this project runs is the pinned postgres:16.10-alpine image in docker-compose.yml, which is not a Maven dependency and is not in scope for this scanner. The JDBC driver org.postgresql:postgresql is a separate dependency and is scanned on its own identity; see its entry below. Scope: test.

TIER 1. io.micrometer:micrometer-registry-prometheus is a Java library that EXPOSES metrics in the Prometheus exposition format. It is not the Prometheus server, which is a separate product written in Go and, in this project, the pinned prom/prometheus:v2.55.1 container in docker-compose.yml. Dependency-Check matched the Micrometer version 1.15.9 against cpe:/a:prometheus:prometheus. The single record this produced, CVE-2026-42154, is a heap exhaustion in the Prometheus server's remote read endpoint /api/v1/read. No such endpoint, and no snappy request decoder, exists in this library; the only surface it provides is the scrape endpoint the server calls.

TIER 1. org.eclipse.angus:angus-activation is the Jakarta ACTIVATION implementation. Dependency-Check matched it to cpe:/a:eclipse:angus_mail, the Jakarta MAIL implementation, and did so at LOW confidence, which the report itself records. The one record that followed, CVE-2025-7962, is an SMTP header injection in Jakarta Mail. Two independent facts make it inapplicable: this is a different artifact, and org.eclipse.angus:angus-mail is not on the dependency graph at all. CardDemo sends no mail; there is no SMTP client anywhere in the target architecture. angus-activation is present only because Jakarta Activation is a transitive requirement of the validation and XML binding stack.

TIER 1. io.opentelemetry.semconv:opentelemetry-semconv is a Java artifact containing nothing but generated semantic convention attribute-key constants. Dependency-Check matched it to cpe:/a:opentelemetry:opentelemetry and attached two records, CVE-2026-24051 and CVE-2026-39883, both at 7.0. Both advisories state their subject in their own first sentence: "OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry". Both are PATH hijacking in resource detection code, naming the Go source file sdk/resource/host_id.go and the ioreg and kenv system commands on Darwin, BSD and Solaris. This artifact is Java, executes no external command, and contains no resource detector. The Java tracing path in this project is micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel with opentelemetry-exporter-otlp, both of which are scanned on their own identities.

TIER 1. Every spring-boot-starter-* artifact is a dependency AGGREGATOR rather than a code artifact. A jar listing at 3.5.11 of all thirteen starters resolved by this build - starter, -web, -actuator, -batch, -data-jpa, -jdbc, -json, -logging, -oauth2-resource-server, -security, -test, -tomcat and -validation - reports ZERO .class entries in every one of them, so no starter can contain a vulnerable class. spring-boot-starter-web is the artifact the scanner flagged first. Its jar was inspected and contains ZERO .class files; its entire content is a POM that pulls in spring-web, spring-webmvc, spring-boot-autoconfigure and the embedded container. Dependency-Check nevertheless assigned it cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot version 3.5.11 and attached the seven Spring Boot product advisories for that version to it, and additionally assigned the generic cpe:/a:web_project:web. No advisory can be exploited through an artifact that contains no code. The jars that DO carry the Spring Boot code, spring-boot, spring-boot-actuator and spring-boot-autoconfigure, are separate dependencies and were evaluated independently in the same scan; nothing is hidden by removing these two CPEs from the aggregator. For the record, the seven advisories in question are also inapplicable on their own terms: CVE-2026-40974 is Cassandra auto-configuration and no Cassandra driver is present; CVE-2026-40971 is RabbitMQ auto-configuration and no AMQP client is present; CVE-2026-22733 requires the CloudFoundry Actuator extension, which requires running on CloudFoundry; CVE-2026-40972 is the spring-boot-devtools remote secret and devtools is not a dependency; CVE-2026-40975 warns that ${random.value} is unfit for secrets, and the one secret this application has, the JWT signing key, is required from the JWT_SECRET environment variable with no generated default; CVE-2026-40973 requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and this application is stateless by architectural mandate, holding no server side session at all; CVE-2026-22731 is discussed in its own Tier 4 entry below.

TIER 1. Same zero-class aggregator argument as the entry immediately above, applied to the other identifier the scanner attached to the starters, for the cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot identifier on both web starters. Both jars were inspected and contain ZERO .class files. The Spring Boot code jars are scanned separately on their own identities.

TIER 1. cpe:/a:web_project:web is a generic identifier for an unrelated product named "web" and was matched purely because these artifact names end in "-web" and their versions happened to align. The correct Spring identifiers on the same artifacts are retained, so both remain fully evaluated against the Spring Framework and Spring Security advisory sets.

TIER 1. cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-modules-java8 was matched against jackson-databind at LOW confidence, which the report records. The java8 modules are separate artifacts (jackson-datatype-jsr310, jackson-module-parameter-names) and are scanned under their own coordinates. The correct identifiers cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-databind and cpe:/a:fasterxml:jackson-core are retained.

TIER 2. All four advisories name classes that live in Log4j CORE or in the Log4j 1 bridge, never in log4j-api: CVE-2026-34478 org.apache.logging.log4j.core.layout.Rfc5424Layout CVE-2026-34479 Log4j1XmlLayout, from the log4j-1.2-api bridge CVE-2026-34480 org.apache.logging.log4j.core.layout.XmlLayout CVE-2026-34481 JsonTemplateLayout, from log4j-layout-template-json Two independent verifications: a grep of the resolved dependency list for log4j-core, log4j-layout-template-json and log4j-1.2-api returns zero matches, and a listing of log4j-api-2.24.3.jar contains zero classes whose name matches Rfc5424Layout, XmlLayout, JsonTemplateLayout or Log4j1XmlLayout. log4j-api is present only as the facade required by log4j-to-slf4j, which routes any Log4j API call into SLF4J and from there into Logback. No Log4j layout, appender or configuration is ever instantiated, because no Log4j implementation exists to instantiate one.

TIER 2. CVE-2026-53914, CVSS 9.8, is code execution "via unsafe deserialization in the BUILD CACHE METADATA" of the JetBrains Kotlin toolchain. The vulnerable component is the Kotlin compiler's incremental build cache, not the runtime standard library. This project contains no Kotlin source file, runs no Kotlin compiler, and produces no Kotlin build cache: it is a Maven Java 25 build whose only compiler plugin is maven-compiler-plugin. kotlin-stdlib is present solely as a runtime scoped transitive of the AWS SDK dependency chain. The attacker controlled artifact the advisory requires cannot exist here because the component that would read it is never invoked. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the Kotlin standard library ships as four sibling artifacts on this graph - kotlin-stdlib, kotlin-stdlib-common, kotlin-stdlib-jdk7 and kotlin-stdlib-jdk8 - and Dependency-Check attaches the same JetBrains Kotlin identifier to every one of them. The argument above is a property of the BUILD (no Kotlin source, no Kotlin compilation, no Kotlin build cache), so it holds identically for all four; the pattern therefore enumerates the four module suffixes explicitly rather than wildcarding the JetBrains group.

TIER 2. Two Spring Framework advisories name classes that belong to Spring Framework MODULES THAT ARE NOT ON THIS DEPENDENCY GRAPH AT ALL. Verified by jar listing at version 6.2.16 and by the resolved dependency tree, which contains spring-aop, spring-aspects, spring-beans, spring-context, spring-core, spring-expression, spring-jcl, spring-jdbc, spring-messaging, spring-orm, spring-test, spring-tx, spring-web and spring-webmvc - and no other org.springframework module: CVE-2026-41855 org.springframework.jms.support.converter. MappingJackson2MessageConverter and JacksonJsonMessageConverter. Zero matches in spring-core and spring-web. spring-jms is not on the dependency graph at all: CardDemo uses SQS through Spring Cloud AWS, not JMS. The "untrusted JMS environment" the advisory requires cannot be reached. CVE-2026-41838 spring-websocket session identifiers. Zero matches for WebSocketSession in spring-core and spring-web; spring-websocket is not on the dependency graph. The target exposes REST and JSON only, with no WebSocket endpoint anywhere in the architecture. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_framework product identifier to EVERY org.springframework module it recognises, so the same two records surface on spring-core, spring-web, spring-tx and spring-webmvc, and would surface on any further module the graph acquires. The argument above is a property of the GRAPH - the module that contains the code is absent - so it holds identically for every org.springframework artifact, and the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group rather than to a hand picked subset that would silently stop matching when the graph shifts. It is deliberately NOT a vendor wide or CVE wildcard entry: exactly two named CVEs are listed.

TIER 2. CVE-2026-40988 is an unbounded inflate of a compressed SAML 2.0 payload in spring-security-saml2-service-provider, using the REDIRECT binding for SAML 2.0 Login or Logout. That artifact is NOT on the dependency graph: the Spring Security artifacts resolved here are core, config, crypto, oauth2-core, oauth2-jose, oauth2-resource-server, web and test, and no saml2 module among them. Authentication in the target is a JWT bearer token issued after a BCrypt password check, replacing the plaintext comparison of the legacy sign-on program; there is no SAML identity provider, no assertion consumer and no SAML endpoint anywhere in the architecture. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_security product identifier to EVERY org.springframework.security module, so this one record surfaces on spring-security-core, spring-security-web, spring-security-oauth2-core, spring-security-oauth2-resource-server and spring-security-test alike. The argument above is a property of the GRAPH - the saml2-service-provider module is absent - so it holds identically for every artifact in the group, and the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group. Exactly one named CVE is listed; this is not a vendor wide entry.

TIER 2. CVE-2026-56816, CVSS 7.5, is unbounded buffering of HTTP/3 reserved frame payloads in io.netty.handler.codec.http3.Http3FrameCodec, reachable only by opening QUIC streams against an HTTP/3 endpoint. The class lives in netty-codec-http3, which is NOT on this dependency graph. The Netty modules that resolve here are exactly buffer, codec, codec-http, codec-http2, common, handler, resolver, transport, transport-classes-epoll and transport-native-unix-common; there is no codec-http3, no QUIC transport and no HTTP/3 listener anywhere in the target, whose only network server is the embedded Tomcat servlet container speaking HTTP/1.1. WHY THIS IS A SUPPRESSION AND NOT AN UPGRADE: Netty is not named by the requirements and was therefore already pinned FORWARD at the root of this build - io.netty:netty-bom 4.1.136.Final in dependencyManagement - which closed thirty-three earlier records by removing the vulnerable code rather than by argument. This one advisory has no fix on the 4.1 line: the vendor fixed it in 4.2.16.Final only, and adopting the 4.2 line would change the transport implementation underneath the AWS SDK asynchronous client, which is a substrate change the requirements do not authorise. Because the affected module is absent from the graph, the 4.1 line carries no exposure. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the record was reported against netty-transport, but Dependency-Check attaches the same Netty product identifier to every io.netty module, so the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE.

TIER 3. Both advisories are defects in jackson-databind's polymorphic deserialization guard and both require POLYMORPHIC TYPING TO BE ENABLED: CVE-2026-54512 PolymorphicTypeValidator is bypassed when polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier is supplied. CVE-2026-54513 BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator.Builder. allowIfSubTypeIsArray() allowlists an array type without validating its component type. Polymorphic typing is not enabled anywhere in this project, and that is enforced rather than merely true today. A search of all main and test sources for JsonTypeInfo, JsonSubTypes, activateDefaultTyping, enableDefaultTyping, PolymorphicTypeValidator and DefaultTyping returns exactly two hits, both in src/test/java/com/cardemo/unit/model/SignOnResponseTest.java, and both belong to a test named "carries no polymorphic type identifier, which would be a deserialisation gadget surface" that ASSERTS THE ABSENCE of @JsonTypeInfo and asserts that no type identifier appears on the wire under any of its usual spellings. That test fails if anyone enables the feature, at which point this suppression must be removed. No ObjectMapper in this project calls activateDefaultTyping, and every DTO is a concrete final shape derived from a BMS symbolic map.

TIER 3. Two Spring Expression Language denial of service advisories that both require, in the advisories' own words, an application that "evaluates USER SUPPLIED Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions": CVE-2026-41850 algorithmic denial of service during evaluation of a specially crafted expression. CVE-2026-41851 denial of service through unbounded SpEL expression cache growth. spring-expression 6.2.16 IS on the runtime classpath - it is a transitive of spring-context and cannot be excluded - so no class absence argument is available and none is claimed. The feature absence argument is exact: this application never parses an expression from caller controlled data. Verified by search across the whole main and test source tree for SpelExpressionParser, ExpressionParser, parseExpression and StandardEvaluationContext: zero occurrences. SpEL reaches this build only through the framework's own internal use in annotation attribute resolution, where every expression is a compile time literal authored in this repository. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: fixed in Spring Framework 6.2.19, inherited through the spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.11 pin that the requirements forbid advancing unilaterally. Remediation is the next parent upgrade. If any future code path ever evaluates a caller supplied expression, this suppression must be removed before that code ships. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_framework product identifier to every org.springframework module, so these records surface on spring-core, spring-web, spring-tx and spring-webmvc. The argument is a property of the APPLICATION, so it holds wherever the record is attached; the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with two named CVEs.

TIER 3. Six Spring Boot 3.5.11 advisories, every one of which names an auto-configuration or a feature that is not present in this application. The affected code is in the spring-boot code jar, so no class absence argument is claimed; each argument below is a verified absence of the feature the advisory requires. CVE-2026-40974 9.8 Cassandra SSL auto-configuration omits hostname verification. There is no Cassandra dependency on the graph: the datastore is PostgreSQL 16 reached through the pgjdbc driver, and a search of the resolved dependency tree for "cassandra" returns zero matches. The auto-configuration cannot activate. CVE-2026-40971 9.1 RabbitMQ auto-configuration omits hostname verification when using an SSL bundle. There is no RabbitMQ or Spring AMQP dependency on the graph - zero matches for "rabbit" - and the target's only queue is an SQS FIFO queue reached through Spring Cloud AWS, replacing the legacy transient data queue. CVE-2026-22733 8.1 authentication bypass when an authenticated endpoint is declared under the path used by the CloudFoundry Actuator endpoints. The CloudFoundry Actuator endpoints are enabled only under a CloudFoundry deployment and its management.cloudfoundry configuration; a search of the whole repository for "cloudfoundry" returns zero matches, and deployment is Docker Compose with Kubernetes and service mesh explicitly out of scope. CVE-2026-40972 7.0 timing attack against the spring-boot-devtools remote secret, leading to class upload and remote code execution. spring-boot-devtools is not a dependency of this build - zero matches on the graph and zero in the build file - so there is no remote secret, no remote restart endpoint and no upload path. CVE-2026-40973 7.0 a local attacker taking control of the ApplicationTemp directory can read session information when server.servlet.session.persistent is true. That property is set nowhere in this repository and its framework default is false. The requirements mandate stateless request handling with no server side session state at all: the legacy pseudo-conversational COMMAREA collapses into JWT claims and request parameters, so there is no session to persist. CVE-2026-40975 7.5 values produced by ${random.value} are unfit for use as secrets. No property placeholder of that form exists anywhere in this repository. The one secret in the system, the JWT signing key, is resolved from an environment variable in every profile with fail fast on absence and no committed default, which is the mechanism the requirements mandate. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: all six are fixed in Spring Boot 3.5.14. This project pins spring-boot-starter-parent at 3.5.11 because the requirements pin it explicitly and forbid advancing it unilaterally, directing instead that the divergence be recorded. This entry is that record. If any of the six features above is ever adopted - Cassandra, RabbitMQ, a CloudFoundry deployment, devtools, persistent sessions or ${random.value} - the corresponding argument collapses and this suppression must be narrowed or removed before that change ships. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: the records were reported against the spring-boot code jar, but Dependency-Check attaches the same cpe:/a:vmware:spring_boot product identifier to spring-boot-autoconfigure, spring-boot-actuator and the starter aggregators as well. The arguments are properties of the APPLICATION and of the RESOLVED BOOT VERSION 3.5.11, identical across the group, so the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with six named CVEs.

TIER 3. CVE-2026-54291, CVSS 8.2 (CVSS v4 only, which is why it does not appear in a v2/v3 filtered reading of the report), in pgjdbc 42.7.4 through 42.7.11: a connection opened with channelBinding=require can be silently DOWNGRADED from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS to plain SCRAM-SHA-256, losing the man in the middle protection that setting is meant to guarantee, because the bundled scram-client returns an empty byte array instead of failing when the server certificate's signature algorithm has no tls-server-end-point binding hash. The advisory's precondition is the connection property channelBinding=require. A search of the whole repository - build file, compose file, environment template, every profile and every Java source - finds no channelBinding property, no sslmode property and no SCRAM configuration of any kind: the JDBC URL carries host, port, database and credentials only. Without channelBinding=require there is no channel binding guarantee to downgrade, so the vulnerable code path is not entered. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: the driver version resolved here, 42.7.10, is inside the affected range. It is not advanced because the requirements record 42.7.10 as the security baseline this gate asserts against and direct that divergence from a recorded version be recorded rather than resolved unilaterally. Compensating control: the database is reached over the private Docker Compose network, never across an untrusted path, and transport security termination is explicitly out of scope for this migration. If channelBinding is ever set to require - which is the correct hardening for a production deployment - the driver must be advanced to a fixed release and this suppression deleted in the same change.

TIER 3. CVE-2026-41848 is a ReDoS in AntPathMatcher that, in the advisory's own words, requires "an attacker ... able to provide a pattern which is then directly or indirectly supplied to one of the following methods in AntPathMatcher". The attacker must control the PATTERN, not the path. In this application every Ant pattern is a compile time literal: the @RequestMapping and @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping values on the eight controllers, and the requestMatchers patterns in the security filter chain. No pattern is read from a request parameter, a request body, a header, a database column or a configuration value that an unauthenticated caller can influence. Request PATHS are matched against those fixed patterns, which is the direction the advisory does not cover. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: fixed in Spring Framework 6.2.19, inherited through the spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.11 pin. Remediation is the next parent upgrade. If a future endpoint ever accepts a caller supplied path pattern, this suppression must be removed before that endpoint ships. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: AntPathMatcher itself lives only in spring-core, but Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_framework product identifier to every org.springframework module, so the same record also surfaces on spring-web, spring-tx and spring-webmvc. The argument above is a property of the APPLICATION - no caller ever supplies a pattern - so it holds identically wherever the record is attached, and the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE.

TIER 3. CVE-2026-47838 concerns SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor mis-reading a malformed X.509 certificate CN, allowing user impersonation. The extractor is reachable only when X.509 CLIENT CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION is configured on the security filter chain. This application authenticates with a JWT bearer token validated by a resource server filter, preceded by a correlation id filter, and issues that token after a BCrypt password check. There is no x509 configuration, no pre-authentication provider and no client certificate trust store anywhere in the target architecture; the embedded container is not configured for mutual TLS and TLS termination is explicitly out of scope. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: fixed in a Spring Security release later than 6.5.8, inherited through the spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.11 pin. Remediation is the next parent upgrade. Adding x509() to the filter chain requires removing this suppression first. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor lives only in spring-security-web - one match there, zero in core, oauth2-core, oauth2-resource-server and test - but Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_security product identifier to every org.springframework.security module, so the record also surfaces on spring-security-oauth2-core and spring-security-test. The argument above is a property of the APPLICATION - x509 authentication is configured nowhere - so it holds identically wherever the record is attached, and the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE.

TIER 3. Fourteen Apache Tomcat advisories concern components that this application does not configure and, in most cases, cannot configure, because it runs an embedded container driven entirely by Spring Boot properties and a Spring Security filter chain, with no web.xml, no server.xml, no valve, no realm, no cluster and no APR or FFM native connector. CVE-2026-43512 digest authentication. The advisory record is itself marked DEPRECATED. No Tomcat authenticator is used at all; authentication is a Spring Security filter. CVE-2026-29145 CLIENT_CERT authentication with soft fail disabled, in Tomcat and Tomcat Native. No client certificate authentication and no tomcat-native on the graph. CVE-2026-43515 improper authorization when multiple method constraints define an HTTP method for the same extension. Requires security constraints in web.xml. There is no web.xml. CVE-2026-55276 special roles and empty authorisation constraints were omitted when the EFFECTIVE WEB.XML was logged. There is no web.xml and no such logging. CVE-2026-53434 CRL configuration on an FFM based connector. No CRL and no FFM connector are configured. CVE-2026-59083 security constraint bypass through URL hex encoding in the REWRITE VALVE. The rewrite valve is not configured. CVE-2026-53404 OR chain condition handling in the REWRITE VALVE. Same. CVE-2026-59084 documentation of secure EncryptInterceptor configuration. EncryptInterceptor belongs to Tomcat clustering, which is not configured; the deployment is a single JAR. CVE-2026-29146 padding oracle in EncryptInterceptor. Same component. CVE-2026-34487 the cloud membership provider for clustering exposed a Kubernetes bearer token in a log. Clustering is not configured and Kubernetes deployment is explicitly out of scope; orchestration stops at Docker Compose. CVE-2026-34483 output escaping in JsonAccessLogValve. That valve is not configured; access logging is not enabled. CVE-2026-43513 case sensitivity in LockOutRealm. No Tomcat realm is configured; lockout is not a Tomcat concern here. CVE-2026-42498 HTTP Authentication header exposed to unexpected hosts during WEBSOCKET authentication. No WebSocket endpoint exists; the surface is REST and JSON only. CVE-2026-29129 configured cipher preference order not preserved. No TLS connector is configured on the embedded container; TLS termination is explicitly out of scope and is recorded as deferred hardening. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: every one of the above is fixed in a Tomcat release later than 10.1.52, which is inherited through the spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.11 pin. Remediation is the next parent upgrade. Enabling any of the named components requires removing the corresponding line here first.

TIER 3. Both records come from httpcore5 5.3.6 SHADED INSIDE com.github.docker-java:docker-java-transport-zerodep, a TEST SCOPE artifact: CVE-2026-54399 unbounded memory in the HTTP/1.1 message parser when a peer sends excessive headers. CVE-2026-54428 unbounded memory in the HTTP/2 HPACK decoder when a peer sends oversized compressed header blocks. Both require a hostile PEER able to send crafted HTTP messages. The only peer this transport ever speaks to is the local Docker daemon, reached over a unix domain socket by Testcontainers while integration tests run. It is never exposed to a network, never reachable by an untrusted party, and never present in the shipped artifact: the Spring Boot fat JAR contains compile and runtime scope only, so this code does not exist in production. The version cannot be remediated here even in principle: httpcore5 is relocated inside the zerodep jar and is therefore not reachable by Maven dependency management, and the parent artifact arrives through Testcontainers 2.0.3, which the requirements pin exactly. RESIDUAL RISK, DISCLOSED: fixed in Apache HttpComponents Core later than 5.4.2. Remediation is a future Testcontainers release that shades a newer core.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. CVE-2026-41842, CVSS 7.5: denial of service when Spring MVC or WebFlux RESOLVES STATIC RESOURCES. The handler it concerns, org.springframework.web.servlet.resource.ResourceHttpRequestHandler, is in spring-webmvc - a jar listing at 6.2.16 finds exactly one match there, and zero in spring-core and zero in spring-web - and spring-webmvc IS on this application's runtime classpath because the target is a Spring MVC REST API. Spring Boot's web auto-configuration registers resource handling by default, so NO CLASS ABSENCE AND NO FEATURE ABSENCE ARGUMENT IS AVAILABLE HERE AND NONE IS CLAIMED. This entry was deliberately re-tiered from a class absence argument to a time boxed acceptance once the scan attributed the record to spring-webmvc itself: asserting absence against the artifact that actually contains the code would have been false. WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED HERE. The fix is Spring Framework 6.2.19. This project declares no Spring Framework version; it is resolved by spring-boot-starter-parent, which the requirements pin explicitly at 3.5.11 and forbid advancing unilaterally, directing instead that the divergence be recorded. This entry is that record. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. The target has no static asset tree to serve: there is no src/main/resources/static, no src/main/resources/public and no META-INF/resources directory in the artifact, verified by directory listing, because the presentation layer is REST and JSON only and 3270 and BMS terminal emulation, HTML front ends and component libraries are all explicitly out of scope. Every endpoint sits behind a correlation id filter then a JWT authentication filter with role based authorisation, and the deployment topology is Docker Compose against LocalStack with no internet exposed listener. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to a release whose managed Spring Framework version is 6.2.19 or later, then DELETE this entry. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_framework product identifier to every org.springframework module, so this record surfaces on spring-core, spring-web, spring-tx and spring-webmvc. The acceptance is a property of the RESOLVED FRAMEWORK VERSION 6.2.16, identical across the group, so the pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01. After that date the record returns and the build fails again. That is deliberate.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. CVE-2026-22732, CVSS 9.1, in spring-security-web 6.5.8: when an application specifies HTTP response headers and Spring Security uses lazy header writing, which is the default, the headers may not be written. The vulnerable class HeaderWriterFilter IS in this artifact and this application does use the standard servlet security filter chain, so no class absence or feature absence argument is available and none is claimed. WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED HERE. The fix is a Spring Security release later than 6.5.8. This project does not declare a Spring Security version: it is resolved by spring-boot-starter-parent, which the requirements pin explicitly at 3.5.11 and which they forbid advancing unilaterally, directing instead that the divergence be recorded. This entry is that record. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. Response security headers are not this application's only defence: authorisation is enforced server side by role, on the request path, before any handler runs, and the target is a JSON API consumed by programmatic clients rather than a browser rendering untrusted markup, so the browser side controls these headers carry are not load bearing here. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to a release whose managed Spring Security version carries the fix, then DELETE this entry. SCOPE OF THE PATTERN: Dependency-Check attaches the single cpe:/a:vmware:spring_security product identifier to every org.springframework.security module, so this one record surfaces on spring-security-web, spring-security-oauth2-core and spring-security-test alike. The acceptance above is a property of the RESOLVED SPRING SECURITY VERSION, 6.5.8, which is identical across every module in the group, so it holds wherever the record is attached. The pattern is scoped to that one Maven group with one named CVE. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01. After that date the record returns and the build fails again. That is deliberate.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. Three Apache Tomcat advisories against tomcat-embed-core 10.1.52 that reach the HTTP/1.1 connector this application actually serves on, and for which no class absence or feature absence argument exists: CVE-2026-41293 9.8 improper input validation. The advisory publishes no component detail, so inapplicability cannot be demonstrated and is not claimed. CVE-2026-24880 7.5 HTTP request smuggling via an invalid chunk extension. Reaches the chunked transfer decoder of the connector in use. CVE-2026-41284 7.5 allocation of resources without limits or throttling. No component detail published. WHY THEY ARE NOT REMEDIATED HERE. All three are fixed in Tomcat releases later than 10.1.52. This project does not declare a Tomcat version: it is resolved by spring-boot-starter-parent, pinned at 3.5.11 by requirement, with unilateral advancement forbidden and recording required instead. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. The container is not internet facing in any supported topology: it is reached through Docker Compose on the developer host, and request rate limiting and TLS termination are both recorded as deferred hardening to be supplied by the edge in a real deployment. Request smuggling additionally requires an intermediary that disagrees with Tomcat about message framing, and there is no proxy in front of the container in this topology. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to a release whose managed Tomcat version is 10.1.56 or later, then DELETE this entry. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. CVE-2026-22731, CVSS 8.1: a Spring Boot Actuator authentication bypass when an authenticated application endpoint is declared under a path already configured as a Health Group additional path. This application does expose Actuator with liveness and readiness health groups, so the feature family is present and no inapplicability is claimed. It is recorded here rather than under the aggregator entry above precisely because it is the one of the seven Spring Boot advisories that cannot be dismissed on its own terms. WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED HERE. Fixed in Spring Boot 3.5.14. The parent is pinned at 3.5.11 by requirement and may not be advanced unilaterally. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. No additional-path is configured for any health group: the groups are served under the standard /actuator/health/{group} paths, and the bypass requires an additional-path that collides with a secured application endpoint. Application endpoints live under /api/**, disjoint from /actuator/**. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to 3.5.14 or later, then DELETE this entry. Configuring management.endpoint.health.group.* .additional-path requires re-examining this record first. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01.

TIER 4 - APPLICABLE. CVE-2026-42198, CVSS 7.5, in the pgjdbc driver org.postgresql:postgresql 42.7.10: a client side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication, in which a malicious server instructs the driver to perform a very large iteration count. The identifier is correct, the version is inside the affected range 42.2.0 to before 42.7.11, and SCRAM-SHA-256 is the authentication method PostgreSQL 16 uses by default, so the code path is genuinely reached on every connection. No inapplicability is claimed. WHY IT IS NOT REMEDIATED HERE. Fixed in 42.7.11. This project does not declare a driver version: 42.7.10 is the version spring-boot-starter-parent 3.5.11 resolves, and the requirements both pin that parent and record 42.7.10 as the resolved driver version, forbidding unilateral advancement. Overriding the property here would diverge from a recorded requirement, so the divergence is recorded instead, which is what the requirements direct. COMPENSATING CONTROLS. The attacker must BE the database server. In every supported topology the server is one this project provisions: the pinned postgres:16.10-alpine service on the compose network, or a Testcontainers instance created by the test itself. The connection URL is supplied by configuration, never by a user, so no caller can redirect the driver at a hostile server. REMEDIATION. Upgrade spring-boot-starter-parent to a release whose managed postgresql version is 42.7.11 or later, then DELETE this entry. This suppression EXPIRES on 2026-11-01.
